entries.title: A two-point cross has 486 recombinants among 1,000 offspring. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: The loci behave as effectively unlinked in this dataset; they may be on different chromosomes or far apart on one chromosome.
options.1: The estimated distance is 9.2 map units, assuming the recombinant classes are correctly identified and similarly viable.
options.2: The pattern supports M as the middle locus, with adjacent interval calculations needed for the map.
options.3: The loci must be on different chromosomes because recombination is near 50%.

entries.title: A fictional height-like trait has a broad range of measurements. Which model should be considered before assuming a simple 3:1 phenotype ratio?

options.0: Several contributing loci and environmental influences
options.1: A continuous range proves one completely dominant locus
options.2: Similarity among relatives rules out environmental effects
options.3: One allele fixes an unchangeable measurement in every environment

entries.title: A genetic variant is modestly associated with a complex trait in one studied population, but the association differs in another. What inference is supported?

options.0: The association needs validation in context and does not by itself prove a universal causal effect.
options.1: The first study proves that changing the variant will cause the same change everywhere.
options.2: The variant determines each individual’s exact trait value.
options.3: A result from one population transfers unchanged to every environment.

entries.title: Genetically matched plants grow to different mean heights under two light conditions. Which comparison best tests an environmental contribution?

options.0: Randomly assign matched plants to the two light treatments while holding other conditions constant
options.1: Compare unrelated plants from two sites that differ in soil, water and light
options.2: Compare genotype labels while recording no light treatment
options.3: Measure the tallest plant from each site and omit the remaining plants

entries.title: Relatives resemble each other for a trait influenced by many genes and their environment. What does this resemblance alone establish?

options.0: It is compatible with shared genetic and environmental influences but does not separate their contributions.
options.1: It proves a single dominant locus controls the trait.
options.2: It rules out an environmental contribution.
options.3: It guarantees identical measurements in every environment.

entries.title: What did Franklin’s X-ray diffraction work contribute?

options.0: Evidence constraining DNA’s helical regularity, dimensions, and molecular arrangement
options.1: A direct colour photograph of DNA bases
options.2: Proof that proteins never carry information
options.3: The complete genetic code

entries.title: A proposed DNA model puts sugar–phosphate backbones at the centre and unpaired bases facing outward. Which correction follows the usual double-helix model?

options.0: Place the backbones externally and complementary paired bases internally.
options.1: Keep the reversed positions because any two strands form the usual helix.
options.2: Replace all backbone bonds with the hydrogen bonds that connect paired bases.
options.3: Treat the central backbone as the normal product of simply separating the strands.

entries.title: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 28% adenine. What percentages of thymine and guanine follow from complementary base pairing?

options.0: 28% thymine and 22% guanine
options.1: 22% thymine and 28% guanine
options.2: 28% thymine and 44% guanine
options.3: 14% thymine and 36% guanine

entries.title: Two strands run in the same direction and bases pair without consistent complementarity. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: The model fails base-ratio and geometry constraints and offers a weak templating mechanism.
options.1: The problem is proved to be tightly crowded phosphate groups in the centre.
options.2: The model integrates chemical, Chargaff, and diffraction evidence and predicts template-based replication.
options.3: Having two strands makes the model correct regardless of direction or base pairing.

entries.title: Why are Okazaki fragments produced?

options.0: Antiparallel templates and 5-prime-to-3-prime synthesis require discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis
options.1: DNA polymerase synthesizes the lagging strand 3-prime to 5-prime
options.2: Helicase cuts chromosomes into genes
options.3: Ligase copies all DNA bases

entries.title: Templates are open, but no new DNA begins at expected initiation sites. Which is one possible mechanism to test, rather than a uniquely proven cause?

options.0: Without primers, DNA polymerase lacks a starting 3-prime end despite available template.
options.1: Synthesis occurred, but ligase-dependent sealing of fragment junctions is incomplete.
options.2: Reduced proofreading increases replication errors while not implying that every mismatch persists or changes phenotype.
options.3: Open DNA proves that polymerase can start without a primer.

entries.title: DNA grown in heavy nitrogen is transferred to light nitrogen. After one complete round of semiconservative replication, which DNA-molecule pattern is expected?

options.0: Each molecule has one old heavy strand and one new light strand
options.1: Half the molecules contain two heavy strands and half contain two light strands
options.2: Each molecule contains two new light strands
options.3: Each strand consists of alternating intact heavy and light nucleotides by a fixed pattern

entries.title: Lagging-strand DNA contains many completed fragments separated by backbone nicks. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: Synthesis occurred, but ligase-dependent sealing of fragment junctions is incomplete.
options.1: Without primers, DNA polymerase lacks a starting 3-prime end despite available template.
options.2: Reduced proofreading increases replication errors while not implying that every mismatch persists or changes phenotype.
options.3: The lagging fragments must have been synthesized 3′→5′ before joining.

entries.title: Which strand does RNA polymerase read?

options.0: The DNA template strand in the 3-prime-to-5-prime direction
options.1: The coding strand in the 5-prime-to-3-prime direction as a template
options.2: Both strands simultaneously for one transcript
options.3: The protein product

entries.title: The gene’s DNA sequence is present, but RNA polymerase occupancy and transcript abundance are low. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The evidence supports reduced transcription initiation rather than deletion of the gene.
options.1: Alternative splicing produced distinct mature transcripts from the same gene region.
options.2: Transcription increased, while translation efficiency or protein degradation may limit protein accumulation.
options.3: An intact DNA sequence must always be transcribed at a high rate.

entries.title: A model cell contains abundant mature mRNA for a gene but little stable protein from that gene. Which next measurements best distinguish two downstream explanations?

options.0: Measure translation rate and protein breakdown rate
options.1: Measure chromosome number and label the gene absent
options.2: Measure promoter activity only and assume mRNA cannot persist
options.3: Measure mRNA again and infer that each transcript makes exactly one protein

entries.title: Two mature RNAs are traced to the same gene region. Both retain exons 1 and 3, while only one retains exon 2. Which explanation fits this processing difference?

options.0: Alternative splicing produced distinct mature transcripts from the same gene region.
options.1: The evidence supports reduced transcription initiation rather than deletion of the gene.
options.2: Transcription increased, while translation efficiency or protein degradation may limit protein accumulation.
options.3: Different mature RNAs prove the cells inherited different chromosome sets.

entries.title: What directly recognizes an mRNA codon during elongation?

options.0: A complementary tRNA anticodon positioned by the ribosome
options.1: A DNA centromere
options.2: A stop amino acid
options.3: RNA polymerase

entries.title: A codon changes from GAA to GAG in the same reading frame; both specify glutamate. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The amino-acid sequence is unchanged, though RNA-level effects remain possible.
options.1: The immediate effect is a missense substitution; protein effect depends on position, chemistry, and structure.
options.2: Downstream codon grouping changes and a premature stop may appear, often producing a larger sequence consequence.
options.3: No change to the peptide proves that no RNA-level effect is possible.

entries.title: Use these code entries: GAA=Glu, GAG=Glu, GUA=Val. Coding DNA changes from 5′-GAA-3′ to 5′-GTA-3′ in the same reading frame. Which peptide-level prediction follows?

options.0: Glu changes to Val because the new RNA codon is GUA
options.1: Glu remains Glu because the new RNA codon is GAG
options.2: The codon becomes a stop because every substitution terminates translation
options.3: The reading frame shifts because one base was substituted

entries.title: A single-base substitution in a coding region changes a codon so that a different amino acid enters the polypeptide. Which immediate consequence follows?

options.0: The immediate effect is a missense substitution; protein effect depends on position, chemistry, and structure.
options.1: The amino-acid sequence is unchanged, though RNA-level effects remain possible.
options.2: Downstream codon grouping changes and a premature stop may appear, often producing a larger sequence consequence.
options.3: Every organism with the substitution must have the same final phenotype.

entries.title: Which statement about mutation is accurate?

options.0: A mutation is a DNA-sequence or chromosome change whose effect depends on location and context
options.1: Every mutation causes disease
options.2: Only environmental chemicals cause mutations
options.3: Somatic mutations are always inherited by offspring

entries.title: A base substitution occurs far from known splice and regulatory regions; RNA and protein measurements are unchanged. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The current evidence supports no detected functional effect under the tested conditions, not proof of no possible effect anywhere.
options.1: Converging recurrence and functional evidence supports a driver role in that tumour context.
options.2: The variant changes risk rather than guaranteeing disease, and counselling must address family information and uncertainty.
options.3: An unchanged assay proves no possible effect in any environment.

entries.title: A mutation appears in a skin-cell lineage but is not detected in the organism’s gametes. Which prediction follows most directly?

options.0: Descendants of that skin cell may inherit it through mitosis
options.1: Each offspring must inherit the mutation through fertilization
options.2: The mutation will be copied into every unrelated cell lineage
options.3: The mutation is automatically synonymous because it is somatic

entries.title: A variant recurs in tumours, activates a growth pathway in cells, and its inhibition reduces growth in matched models. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: Converging recurrence and functional evidence supports a possible contribution to growth in the studied tumour model.
options.1: The measurements demonstrate no detected functional difference.
options.2: The experiment establishes an individual’s inherited disease probability.
options.3: The same variant guarantees identical growth effects and treatment response in every tumour.

entries.title: What does DNA ligase do in recombinant-DNA construction?

options.0: It seals phosphodiester-bond breaks between compatible DNA ends
options.1: It recognizes every target gene
options.2: It copies RNA into protein
options.3: It selects transformed cells

entries.title: Colonies survive selection, but insert-specific PCR produces no product. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The result is consistent with a missing target insert or a failed insert assay; vector-only background is one possibility that requires controls.
options.1: Incorrect orientation or regulatory design can explain presence without expected transcription.
options.2: Translation, folding, modification, sequence error, or assay conditions remain possible after DNA and RNA verification.
options.3: Surviving selection proves the target insert is present and expressed.

entries.title: Colonies grow on antibiotic selection after receiving a plasmid intended to carry an inserted gene. Which next test most directly verifies that the desired insert has the intended sequence?

options.0: Sequence the insert and its junctions in a selected colony
options.1: Count colonies on the same selection plate again
options.2: Measure the antibiotic concentration without examining DNA
options.3: Infer the insert sequence from colony colour without a validated reporter

entries.title: Insert DNA is present, but transcript from the intended promoter is absent. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: Incorrect orientation or regulatory design can explain presence without expected transcription.
options.1: The selectable vector entered cells, but the target insert is absent; vector-only background is plausible.
options.2: Translation, folding, modification, sequence error, or assay conditions remain possible after DNA and RNA verification.
options.3: An insert must always be transcribed because its DNA is present.

entries.title: What does PCR do?

options.0: It amplifies selected DNA regions using primers and repeated cycles
options.1: It directly proves a person’s identity
options.2: It separates proteins by size
options.3: It translates DNA into amino acids

entries.title: A partial mixed sample includes alleles consistent with a person and with many possible relatives or unrelated contributors. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The partial match leaves multiple possible sources and needs further informative markers and quality checks.
options.1: The evidence already ranks one defined parent–child model over an unrelated model.
options.2: The result is a complete ancestry estimate.
options.3: One matching allele uniquely identifies the source of the whole sample.

entries.title: Two samples have matching band positions at one DNA marker. Which extension most improves discrimination between possible sources?

options.0: Compare additional informative independent markers with suitable controls
options.1: Repeat the same marker and report the matching bands as a whole-genome identity
options.2: Use band brightness alone as a unique inherited genotype
options.3: Discard samples from relatives because relatives cannot share marker alleles

entries.title: A child and tested adult share marker patterns more likely under one stated biological relationship than under an unrelated model. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: The result supports the tested relationship model probabilistically and depends on reference, mutation, and alternative-relative assumptions.
options.1: The evidence cannot identify one source without mixture modelling, population frequencies, quality evidence, and alternatives.
options.2: The estimate is model- and reference-dependent and should not be equated with culture, citizenship, Indigenous belonging, or complete family history.
options.3: The favored relationship is certain because all alternatives are impossible.

entries.title: What is the purpose of a negative control?

options.0: To reveal background signal or contamination when the target condition is absent
options.1: To guarantee the hypothesis is correct
options.2: To increase every measured value
options.3: To replace replication

entries.title: A PCR investigation finds products in every tube, including unexpected samples, but no blank control was run. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: Contamination cannot be assessed; a negative control is needed before interpreting sample products.
options.1: The small deviation is compatible with sampling variation; a larger repeated sample and model check are needed.
options.2: The design supports auditable analysis, though model applicability and measurement uncertainty still require discussion.
options.3: A band in every sample proves that every sample has the uncontaminated target.

entries.title: For a predicted 1:2:1 genotype ratio, sample 1 has counts 3 AA, 5 Aa and 2 aa; sample 2 has 24 AA, 51 Aa and 25 aa. Which comparison is appropriate?

options.0: Compare frequencies with 0.25, 0.50 and 0.25, while considering the different sample sizes
options.1: Compare only the raw Aa counts, 5 and 51, to decide which cross has stronger dominance
options.2: Require every sample of ten to contain exactly 2.5 AA individuals
options.3: Treat the larger sample as proof that gametes always meet in a fixed sequence

entries.title: Six offspring are used to reject a 3:1 model because the observed ratio is 4:2. Which explanation is most consistent with this new evidence?

options.0: The small deviation is compatible with sampling variation; a larger repeated sample and model check are needed.
options.1: Contamination cannot be assessed; a negative control is needed before interpreting sample products.
options.2: The design supports auditable analysis, though model applicability and measurement uncertainty still require discussion.
options.3: The six offspring must exactly match 3:1 or segregation is false.

entries.title: A fictional crop-research project tests a genetic construct intended to support food production during drought. Use the pilot observations to distinguish the intended benefit, an unintended human consequence and a possible environmental consequence. Explain how further research could support a sustainable society, economy and environment. State an initial research priority. A grower then objects that trial costs make participation difficult. Revise the priority or justify retaining it with an adaptation. Name what to monitor before expansion, and explain why this pilot does not establish one cause or a final sustainability verdict.
A variant lies at a splice boundary, an exon is missing from mature RNA, and protein abundance is low. Which explanation best connects this evidence to the lesson mechanism?

options.0: The sequence, RNA, and protein evidence converge on disrupted splicing; cellular and organism outcomes still require evidence.
options.1: Chromosome-location and linkage evidence support an autosomal linked explanation over the initial pedigree shortcut.
options.2: Functional convergence supports a driver role while heterogeneity and clinical response remain uncertain.
options.3: The three observations prove a unique cause and every later phenotype.

entries.title: A transformed cell contains the verified insert but no detectable intended protein. Which investigation best separates an expression problem from a DNA-insert problem?

options.0: Measure gene-specific mRNA and protein under the intended expression conditions
options.1: Repeat the insert sequence and infer protein activity without measuring it
options.2: Compare antibiotic resistance only, because resistance proves every gene is expressed
options.3: Count DNA bands and interpret the count as the number of active proteins

entries.title: In a fictional model-organism investigation, a preliminary sketch labels two studied loci as X-linked. Verified physical evidence locates both on one autosome, and a phased test cross finds a large excess of parental combinations with low recombination. What should be revised?

options.0: Chromosome-location and linkage evidence support an autosomal linked explanation over the initial pedigree shortcut.
options.1: The sequence, RNA, and protein evidence converge on disrupted splicing; cellular and organism outcomes still require evidence.
options.2: Functional convergence supports a driver role while heterogeneity and clinical response remain uncertain.
options.3: All genes in the organism must have the same linkage pattern.

entries.title: A diploid cell has 8 chromosomes before DNA replication. Give chromosome, chromatid and set counts before and after replication, then distinguish homologues from sisters.

Construct a bar graph for the supplied illustrative counts: interphase 72, prophase 12, metaphase 6, anaphase 4, and telophase/cytokinesis 6. Choose labelled axes and a scale. Calculate mitotic index and explain what additional assumptions a phase-duration estimate requires.

Compare cytoplasmic division in a typical animal cell and a typical plant cell. Name the boundary-forming structure and direction of its development in each. Both images show two daughter nuclear regions, but only one shows a complete boundary between them. Explain why counting nuclei alone cannot establish the number of separate cells.
Track a cell with two homologous chromosome pairs through meiosis I and II. Name what separates and give chromosome numbers in each product.
Compare nondisjunction of one homologous pair in meiosis I with nondisjunction in only one meiosis II cell. Give the four product categories for the tracked chromosome.
Trace a plant life cycle from diploid sporophyte back to diploid sporophyte, labelling meiosis, mitosis and fertilization.
A fictional plant trait has alleles A and a with complete dominance. Compare AA, Aa and aa and explain why these symbols do not predict population frequency.
Explain how segregation connects an Aa parent's meiosis to an Aa × Aa Punnett square. Predict genotype and phenotype probabilities under complete dominance.
For AaBb × AaBb with independently assorting loci and complete dominance, calculate P(aabb) and P(A_bb). Explain each multiplication.
Cross Iᴬi with Iᴮi in the simplified ABO model. List gametes, offspring genotypes and phenotypes with probabilities; distinguish codominance from multiple alleles.
Under a fully penetrant autosomal recessive model, two unaffected parents have an affected child. Give parent genotypes and the carrier probability for another child known to be unaffected.

An AB/ab heterozygote is test-crossed with ab/ab, producing 40 AB, 40 ab, 10 Ab and 10 aB gamete-derived offspring. Calculate recombination frequency. In a separate mapping dataset, interpret distances A–B=14, B–C=6 and A–C=20 map units.
Write the complementary strand paired with 5′-ATGC-3′, then write that complementary sequence in its own 5′→3′ direction. Name one historical constraint supporting the model.
At a replication fork, explain why both new strands grow 5′→3′ even though one is made in fragments. Name the roles of primer, polymerase and ligase.
Given coding DNA 5′-ATGGAATTTTAA-3′, write aligned template DNA and the mRNA 5′→3′. Explain which strand RNA polymerase reads.
Use mRNA 5′-AUG GAA UUU UAA-3′ in the indicated start frame. Write the peptide and an anticodon paired with GAA; explain termination.
Compare coding sequences 5′-ATG GAA TTT TAA-3′ and 5′-ATG GAG TTT TAA-3′ in the same frame. Then predict the consequence of adding one base immediately after ATG.
A negative PCR control has a band, and two sample bands are similar in size. Explain what can be concluded and identify a next check.

Compare mitosis and meiosis starting from an unreplicated diploid cell with 2n=6. Assume successful replication, division and cytoplasmic separation in a simplified model. Make seven labelled comparison rows: DNA replications, nuclear divisions, homologue pairing, structures separated, product number, product ploidy/chromosome count, and genetic similarity. Explain why “all products are guaranteed genetically identical” is too strong for either process.
Classify authentic cell images using chromosome alignment or separation. Explain how uncertain images should be recorded.
Compare a plant alternation-of-generations cycle with polyp/medusa phases in a cnidarian model.
For AaBb × aabb under independent assortment, construct gametes and the four expected offspring classes.
Cross a carrier mother XᴬXᵃ with an unaffected father XᴬY in a simple X-linked recessive model. Give risk among sons and among all children under equal sex probability.
A three-gene map has distances X–Y=8, Y–Z=5 and X–Z=13. Give order and one limit of pairwise mapping.
For template 3′-TAC CTT AAA ATT-5′, transcribe 5′→3′ and translate the indicated start frame.
Contrast a base substitution, a one-base insertion and a three-base insertion within a coding region.

These invented plant samples compare three different homologous regions. Within each panel, all sequences run 5′→3′ and positions are already aligned with equal coverage and no gaps. Count substitutions from that panel’s reference for X, Y and Z, and rank their similarity separately for each panel. For this fictional species, assume nuclear inheritance from both parents and mitochondrial/chloroplast inheritance through one parent. Explain a conditional relatedness inference, why the rankings can differ, and two checks or limits before making a whole-organism ancestry claim. Do not align different panels to each other.

Use one visible feature from the authentic images and keep it separate from the supplied synthetic counts. Calculate mitotic index and a conditional interphase-duration estimate using the 20-hour model. State a testable question and prediction about phase counts, then design a repeated comparison with consistent observation rules. A reviewer claims, “A large mitotic fraction proves rapid population growth.” Give an alternative explanation, revise that claim, and name a measurement that would distinguish the explanations.

Use the supplied Aa×Aa samples to state a testable question and prediction about sample size and genotype proportions. Compare observed and expected counts for one small and one large sample. Design repeated comparisons with parental genotypes, scoring and inheritance assumptions controlled. A reviewer claims, “Any departure from 1:2:1 disproves segregation.” Give another possible source of disagreement, revise the claim, and identify a check that would distinguish the explanations. Do not predict that every larger sample must be closer.

Use the supplied coding sequences and fragment measurements to ask a testable question and predict which method can distinguish a one-base change. Cite a sequence contrast and the complete fragment totals for reference and insertion models. Design a repeated comparison with suitable controls and consistent conditions. A reviewer claims, “Equal apparent gel-band size proves identical sequence.” Give an alternative explanation for similar bands, revise that claim and identify the more discriminating evidence. Keep the short coding excerpt separate from the measured larger fragments.

A model cell with 2n=4 completes normal meiosis I. One chromosome fails to separate its sisters in one of the two meiosis-II cells; the other cell divides normally. Give chromosome counts in all four products and compare the pattern with one meiosis-I nondisjunction event.

Both parents are AB/ab, with complete dominance at each locus. Change the model from independent assortment to complete linkage with no crossing over. Calculate P(aabb) and P(A_bb), and identify the offspring class that would disprove complete linkage in this cross.

Under full penetrance, two unaffected parents with an affected recessive child must both be Aa. Now allow some aa people to be unaffected. Does the usual 2/3 carrier probability for an unaffected sibling still follow? Explain what extra information is needed.

An AB/ab heterozygote is test-crossed with ab/ab, yielding 40 AB, 40 ab, 10 Ab and 10 aB gamete-derived offspring. A learner treats 20% recombination as an exact count of crossover events. Explain how hidden exchanges can break that inference and propose a more informative cross.
A sequence is now labelled TEMPLATE 5′-ATGGAATTTTAA-3′, rather than coding DNA. Write the RNA 5′→3′ and explain why simply replacing T with U gives the wrong result.

A repeated PCR run has a blank negative control and a successful positive control. Two samples produce bands of the same apparent size. Which earlier control concern is reduced, which identity claim remains unsupported, and what further evidence could test sequence identity?
